description: Automation Health Dashboard — composite view of UI Bridge automation quality. Shows health score gauge, improvement recommendations, element reliability heatmap, action performance baselines, failure taxonomy, automation regressions, stall frequency, intervention effectiveness, and annotation gaps. Powered by cross-run analytics from ui_bridge_events (element interactions persisted per action with duration, success, error). Data flows: action handler → insert_ui_bridge_event → SQLite → 17 analytics SQL queries → 13 MCP endpoints → React hooks → dashboard panels. Health score is a weighted composite: 0.30 * element_success_rate + 0.25 * (1 - regression_rate) + 0.25 * (1 - stall_frequency) + 0.20 base. Recommendations are rule-based: flaky elements → add data-testid, stalls → increase settle_delay, unannotated → add annotations, high failure rate → review taxonomy.

groups.name: Dashboard Layout and Navigation
groups.description: The dashboard has a header with title, time range selector (24h/7d/30d), and refresh button. Below is a 5-row responsive grid of analytics panels. All panels use consistent card styling (bg-card, rounded-lg, border).

Users can select 24-hour time range
Users can select 7-day time range (default)

groups.name: Automation Health Score
groups.description: Large centered numeric score (0-100) with color coding (green >= 90, yellow >= 70, orange >= 50, red < 50) and label (Excellent/Good/Fair/Poor). Below the score: breakdown of element_success_rate, regression_rate, stall_frequency, total_interactions, unique_elements. Score computed server-side from ui_bridge_events via compute_automation_health_score(). Backed by GET /ui-bridge/analytics/health-score.

assertions.description: The health score card is identifiable by its heading

target.label: Health score card heading with Activity icon

assertions.description: The element success rate metric is displayed in the breakdown
The regression rate metric shows what fraction of elements degraded between runs
The stall frequency metric shows how often the UI got stuck during automation
The total interactions count shows how many UI Bridge actions have been recorded

The score number uses green for >= 90, yellow for >= 70, orange for >= 50, red for < 50. The label matches: Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor respectively. This color coding communicates automation quality at a glance.

target.label: Health score with color-coded quality indicator

groups.name: Improvement Recommendations
groups.description: Prioritized list of actionable recommendations generated by generate_recommendations(). Each has a numbered priority badge, color-coded category (selectors=blue, performance=orange, annotations=purple, reliability=red), a message, and an impact statement. Categories correspond to: flaky_element_count > 3 → selectors, stall_count > 2 → performance, unannotated > 5 → annotations, failure_rate > 10% → reliability. Backed by GET /ui-bridge/analytics/recommendations.

groups.name: Automation Regressions
groups.description: Detects element+action pairs that degraded between the older and newer halves of recent events. Uses NTILE(2) window function to split events into prior/recent halves. Shows element_id, action, prior success rate (green), recent success rate (red), and delta (red, bold). Only shows pairs with >= 4 events and > 10% degradation. Backed by GET /ui-bridge/analytics/regressions.

Tables use consistent column styling (text-xs text-muted-foreground headers, hover:bg-muted/50 rows). Color thresholds are uniform: green >= 95%, yellow >= 80%, red < 80% for success rates. groups.name: Backend Data Pipeline
groups.description: Architecture: UI Bridge action handlers (mcp/ui_bridge.rs, mcp/sdk_client.rs) persist events to ui_bridge_events table via insert_ui_bridge_event() when ?task_run_id= query param is present. Events flow through 17 SQL query functions in database/ui_bridge_ops.rs, exposed via 13 MCP HTTP endpoints under /ui-bridge/analytics/*. The knowledge graph (reflection/graph_engine.rs) loads UIElement nodes and InteractedWith edges for causal analysis. The stall detector (orchestration_loop/stall_detector.rs) fetches /ui-bridge/control/health-signals to detect UIStuck patterns. Token attribution flows through phase_token_usage.target_app via get_active_sdk_app_name(). CTR auto-seeding pushes element reliability data to SDK apps on connect via push_ctr_reliability_to_sdk().
